newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DSM dividend woos long-term investors.
newsitem.headline: DSM dividend woos long-term investors.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group DSM said on Tuesday it had decided to amend its dividend policy in order to woo long-term investors.

"This (move) would make our stock more attractive to stay in (investors') portfolios...we want to create a more solid, stable shareholders' base," finance director Louk Ligthart told a results news conference.
If price-earnings ratios of the stock increased as a result this would be a bonus, Ligthart added.
DSM earlier said it lifted its dividend to 9.0 guilders from 8.0 on 1996 net profit down 351 million guilders at 720 million.

Under the revised dividend policy, dividends to ordinary shareholders would be pegged at 16-20 percent of cashflow from ordinary activites after deduction of the dividend to cumulative preference shareholders, DSM said.
This would result in a more predictable pay-out, it said.

From 1996 onwards pay-outs may also be made in shares, but in order to prevent dilution of profits per share, DSM would buy back at least an equivalent number of shares to that paid out in the form of a stock dividend, Ligthart said.
DSM could buy back more if equity levls rose to such an extent they undermined the targeted 15 percent return on equity.
DSM paid a dividend to cumulative preference shareholders of 28 million guilders over 1996. This would rise to 35 million guilders annually over the years 1997-2005, the company said.
